extracted.intended_audience: stand-up comedians, comedy writers, and performers studying Jerry Seinfeld's craft
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for writing and performing short, precise stand-up jokes and bits, drawing on Seinfeld's remarks about premise, wording, setup/punchline calibration, and audience focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subtraction of words
rubrics_metrics.description: "The greatest skill in comedy is the SUBTRACTION of words."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trim language to the minimum necessary. The page emphasizes economy of wording as a core craft doctrine — remove anything that doesn't drive the joke. (Also echoed in the working rubric: "Have you subtracted enough words?")

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience as final arbiter
rubrics_metrics.description: "The audience is the only opinion that matters."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize what actually gets laughs over personal taste or peer judgments. Test material on real audiences and let their responses guide edits and choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Believability/commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: "If you don't believe what you're saying, they won't believe you."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performer must fully commit to the premise and delivery; lack of conviction undermines the joke. This covers both truthful-feeling performance and internal acceptance of the material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joke as a small machine
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Think of jokes as precise mechanisms where each part has a function. Design setups, beats, words, and punchlines to work together efficiently; remove parts that don't contribute to the mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funny is the currency
rubrics_metrics.description: "Funny is the only currency I deal in."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure choices by whether they generate laughs; avoid elevating style or intellectual cleverness above actual funniness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Premise: obsess about small irritations
rubrics_metrics.description: Seinfeld talks about getting OBSESSED with small irritations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose premises rooted in small, relatable annoyances and sit with them to mine details and angles. Obsession helps surface specific, relatable comic material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sit with the premise to find layers
rubrics_metrics.description: The longer he sits with the irritation, the more layers of joke he finds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow time for iterative thinking—revisiting a premise reveals deeper angles, escalations, and alternate punchlines. This is explicitly listed as a working rubric item: "Have you sat with the premise long enough to find the LAYERS?"

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to boring detail
rubrics_metrics.description: "Boring is funny if you commit to how boring it is."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Holding precisely to mundane or 'boring' details can create contrast and tension that yields laughs; commitment to the detail is essential. (Also appears in working rubric: "Are you committed to the boring detail?")

rubrics_metrics.name: Cliff/setup-to-punchline gap calibration
rubrics_metrics.description: "The setup creates the cliff edge. The audience must JUMP to the punchline. If the cliff is too narrow, they don't believe they need to jump. If too wide, they fall in the ravine and don't laugh."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design the setup so it creates a believable necessity for the audience to make the inference to the punchline, but keep the inference attainable. Calibrate surprise: enough distance to be unexpected, not so much that it's unintelligible. (Working rubric parallels: "Is the cliff exactly leapable for the room?")

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance raw feeling with filtered language
rubrics_metrics.description: Larry David: "Comedy comes from the place where you can't control what you're feeling." Seinfeld: "Yeah, but you can control how you describe it. That's the writing."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use authentic, uncontrolled emotion as the source material but craft and filter the language deliberately. Let feeling inform content; let writing shape and sharpen it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surprise: give the audience something they didn't know they were waiting for
rubrics_metrics.description: Norm Macdonald: "The funniest thing is the thing the audience didn't know they were waiting for."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for punchlines or turns that subvert audience expectations in a way that feels inevitable in retrospect. Surprising but structurally supported payoffs tend to land strongly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Let interesting storytelling create humor
rubrics_metrics.description: Norm: "I don't try to be funny. I try to tell a story I find interesting and let the funny happen."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize telling a story or pursuing an interesting comic idea rather than forcing jokes; sustained interest often produces organic humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have you sat with the premise long enough to find the LAYERS?
rubrics_metrics.description: Working rubric item: "Have you sat with the premise long enough to find the LAYERS?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit checklist item encouraging time and iteration on a premise to uncover additional comedic angles and escalations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have you subtracted enough words?
rubrics_metrics.description: Working rubric item: "Have you subtracted enough words?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit checklist item directing writers/performers to edit ruthlessly for economy and precision in wording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the cliff exactly leapable for the room?
rubrics_metrics.description: Working rubric item: "Is the cliff exactly leapable for the room?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the setup-to-punchline gap fits the specific audience; calibrate material to the crowd's knowledge, speed, and expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Are you committed to the boring detail?
rubrics_metrics.description: Working rubric item: "Are you committed to the boring detail?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checklist reminder to maintain precise, committed delivery on mundane specifics when that's the comedic focal point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Are you in service of the audience's laugh, not your own taste?
rubrics_metrics.description: Working rubric item: "Are you in service of the audience's laugh, not your own taste?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-check to avoid prioritizing personal cleverness or niche preferences over material that produces broad laughs for the audience at hand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the joke a small, precise machine?
rubrics_metrics.description: Working rubric item: "Is the joke a small, precise machine?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether every element of the joke contributes to its operation; remove redundancy and ensure structural efficiency.
